entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Robert Somercotes (fl. 1241) was an English Cardinal of significant regional impact.


He took part in the Papal conclave of 1241, but died during it, fueling rumors of poisoning to prevent his election.







 Somercotes' tenure as a cardinal was short-lived but notable for its connections to high-level ecclesiastical politics and the intrigue surrounding his potential papability.







 His legacy as a major figure in the conclave has endured through scholarly analysis and historical reevaluation of the events surrounding his death.







 Despite the brevity of his time as a cardinal, Somercotes' actions had a lasting impact on the course of papal succession and the politics of the Catholic Church during the 13th century.
